Fig. 3
Pyruvate dehydrogenase and the TCA cycle. Within the mitochondria pyruvate is decarboxylated to form Acetyl CoA which, together with
Acetyl CoA from the catabolism of other fuels, enters the TCA cycle. Acetyl CoA (2 C) combines with oxaloacetate (4 C) to form citrate (6 C). In
a series of reactions two carbons are lost as CO2 with the production of 2 NADH, 1 FADH2 and a GTP to regenerate the oxaloacetate.
